content.text: Korean series and Japanese anime are some of the most popular things on Netflix all over the world, including Oman and the Gulf. Here are the best Korean series on Netflix and the best Netflix anime, plus the live-action versions of famous anime.
Best Korean series on Netflix
Squid Game
The survival drama that made the whole world talk about Korean series on Netflix. After the first season, Squid Game 2 and the final season complete the story of player 456.
All of Us Are Dead
Students fight to survive a zombie outbreak in their high school. Scary, fast and full of heart.
Money Heist: Korea – Joint Economic Area

The Korean remake of Money Heist moves the story to a future where North and South Korea share a joint economic area, and the team robs the new unified mint. Interesting even if you know the Spanish original.
Single’s Inferno
A Korean dating show where singles are left on a deserted island and can only escape to "paradise" as a couple. Light, funny and very addictive.
XO, Kitty
Kitty Song Covey from To All the Boys moves to a school in Seoul to find her long-distance boyfriend. A fun teen romance that feels like a K-drama.
Best anime on Netflix
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners

From Studio Trigger and set in the world of the game Cyberpunk 2077, this cyberpunk anime follows a street kid in Night City who becomes a mercenary. Colourful, violent and emotional; many fans call it one of the best Netflix anime.
Record of Ragnarok
The gods decide to end humanity, and thirteen legendary humans fight thirteen gods one-on-one for the future of mankind. Record of Ragnarok anime is pure battle entertainment.
Lookism
A bullied high-school student wakes up with a second, perfect body. Lookism anime, based on a popular webtoon, talks about appearance, bullying and friendship.
Bubble
Bubble is one of the most beautiful anime movies on Netflix: in a Tokyo flooded and covered in strange bubbles, young parkour teams race across the ruins of the city.
Anime brought to life: live-action on Netflix

items: One Piece: the live-action One Piece follows Luffy and the Straw Hat crew; the Netflix One Piece series surprised even long-time fans.
Avatar: The Last Airbender: the live-action Avatar retells Aang’s journey to master all four elements.
Death Note: the 2017 Netflix film is a different take on the famous anime about a notebook that kills.
